Feature + interface designReady

    Select any step to read at your own pace.

    A clear plan for the next model.

    For a team invitation feature, the planner defines roles and expiry rules. The implementer receives a focused brief, relevant files, and acceptance checks. Design guidance shapes the invitation states; review checks the result.

    What gets handed over

    • Decisions: owner permissions and single-use invites.
    • Assignment: server checks, invitation lifecycle, and interface states.
    • Verification: unauthorized actions, expired links, and keyboard access.

    You describe the outcome once. Kishu loads the relevant guidance.

    Illustrative scenarios, not live agent runs. Model profiles are examples; your host’s available models and saved preferences determine the actual choices.

    Big thinking.
    Where it counts.

    A high-cost model doesn’t need to write every line. Put deeper reasoning on the tricky decisions, and let an efficient coding model carry the plan forward.

    • Focus premium-model tokens. Reserve expensive thinking for the parts that need it.
    • Cut repeated discovery. Give the builder a concise brief, relevant context, and clear checks.
    • Move independent work together. Parallelize separate assignments after agreeing the shared plan.

    The mix can reduce cost and waiting. Actual savings depend on the task, model prices, context, and coordination overhead.

    Explore Kishu on GitHub

    A little setup. Then, just ask.

    1. Clone the repo and install the plugin. 

    git clone https://github.com/SPDUK/kishu-stack.git
cd kishu-stack
python scripts/kishu.py install --harness codex

    2. Start a new chat. Give Kishu a challenge.

    $kishu:kishu-mode

    Select Kishu through /skills, or use the command above. Python 3.11+ and Git are needed for installation.

    Kishu, explained.

    The practical details: where it works, how you choose your models, and what the workflow adds.

    What is Kishu?

    Kishu is an open-source workflow plugin for AI coding agents. It brings task routing, customizable model roles, design guidance, and ADHD-aware communication together in one entrypoint: Kishu mode.

    Which coding agents does Kishu support?

    Kishu provides native plugin entrypoints for Codex, Cursor, and Claude Code, plus a standalone skill export. It works inside your existing agent with the code and tools available in that environment.

    Can I choose different AI models for different roles?

    Yes. Kishu setup helps you choose supported models and reasoning effort for planning, implementation, review, and other roles. Saved preferences guide delegation when it is useful. Available models depend on your host; role preferences do not change the model running your current chat.

    Can model routing reduce coding costs or save time?

    It can concentrate expensive reasoning on difficult decisions, give efficient coding models a focused brief, and let independent assignments run in parallel. Savings depend on the task, model prices, context, and coordination overhead. The examples on this site are illustrative, not benchmarks.

    What do pstack and Impeccable do in Kishu?

    pstack provides the engineering playbooks behind Kishu’s routing and handoffs. Impeccable provides the foundation for its design guidance. Kishu adapts these foundations with its own preferences for scope, model choices, useful checks, and clear communication; i-have-adhd informs its communication style.

    Good roots.
    A Kishu point of view.

    Kishu brings three open-source foundations together with its own working preferences: care where it counts, less process to manage, and your choices at the center.
